description: Performance and scalability enhancements: Add an async HTTP client wrapper (utils/async_requester.py) with connection pooling, implement a concurrent scan worker pool (core/scan_pool.py) with configurable concurrency, and add a rate limiter with token bucket algorithm. These provide the infrastructure for async I/O and better concurrency without requiring httpx/aiohttp (uses concurrent.futures and threading for stdlib-only operation).
steps: Create utils/async_requester.py - An async-capable request dispatcher that wraps the existing Requester with connection pooling and concurrent request execution. Implements: ConnectionPool class (manages a pool of reusable sessions with max_connections limit, checkout/return pattern, health checks), AsyncRequestDispatcher class (submits requests to a ThreadPoolExecutor, supports batch_request for multiple URLs, uses futures for non-blocking waits), RateLimiter class (token bucket algorithm with configurable rate and burst). All type-hinted with Python 3.10+ syntax.

Create core/scan_pool.py - A worker pool for concurrent module execution. Implements: ScanWorkerPool class that accepts a list of (module, url, method, param, value) tasks and executes them with bounded concurrency using ThreadPoolExecutor. Features: configurable max_workers, task prioritization (critical vulns first), graceful shutdown, progress tracking callback, error isolation (one module crash doesn't kill others), result aggregation. Type-hinted throughout.

Add type hints to utils/requester.py - Add comprehensive type annotations to the existing ResponseCache class and add a ConnectionPoolManager class that manages requests.Session objects with connection pooling (urllib3 pool_connections, pool_maxsize). Add return type annotations to all public methods.

Create tests/test_async_requester.py with 12+ tests covering: ConnectionPool init/checkout/return/exhaustion, RateLimiter token bucket behavior (allows burst then throttles), AsyncRequestDispatcher batch execution, timeout handling, pool cleanup.

Create tests/test_scan_pool.py with 10+ tests covering: ScanWorkerPool init, task submission, concurrent execution verification (timing), error isolation, graceful shutdown, progress callback invocation, result collection.
acceptance_criteria: RateLimiter correctly implements token bucket (tests prove burst allowance + throttling)
ConnectionPool enforces max_connections limit (tests prove blocking when pool exhausted)
ScanWorkerPool isolates module errors (one failure doesn't crash others)
All test files pass pytest without external dependencies
All new code has comprehensive type hints (no Any escapes except where truly needed)
verification: python -m py_compile utils/async_requester.py && python -m py_compile core/scan_pool.py
python -m mypy utils/async_requester.py core/scan_pool.py --ignore-missing-imports --no-error-summary 2>&1 | grep -c 'error' || true
findings: All 38 tests pass (24 in test_async_requester, 14 in test_scan_pool). py_compile passes for all new files. ruff linter passes. mypy passes on utils/async_requester.py and core/scan_pool.py with no errors (existing project has 170+ pre-existing mypy errors in other files). Used importlib.util to load core/scan_pool.py in tests to bypass core/__init__.py which triggers yaml dependency. Replaced the pre-existing httpx-based utils/async_requester.py with a stdlib-only implementation.
